episode_title: Dell Computers: Michael Dell. The College Dropout Who Took on IBM (2018)

real_qa.q: How did Michael Dell discover married couples were more likely to buy newspaper subscriptions?
real_qa.r: Dell observed through his work calling random people that those getting married were much more likely to buy the newspaper. He then discovered that marriage license applications were public information available at the county courthouse, including the address where the license would be sent. He used this data to send direct mail campaigns to newlyweds in a 16 county area surrounding Harris County, Texas.
real_qa.requete: Michael Dell newspaper subscriptions marriage registry

real_qa.q: What was the key difference between Dell computers and IBM computers in the mid-1980s?
real_qa.r: IBM sold a 6 megahertz 286 computer for $3,995, while Dell introduced a 12 megahertz 286-based computer and sold it for $1,995. Dell's computer was twice as fast and half the price because they had clever engineers, created an efficient supply chain with daily or hourly parts delivery, and benefited from lower material costs as technology prices fell.

real_qa.q: How much revenue was Dell Computer Corporation generating when Michael Dell was 21 years old?
real_qa.r: When Michael Dell was 21 years old, Dell Computer Corporation was doing $66 million in sales that year. At that time, Dell was already competing with IBM and had expanded beyond dorm room operations to a proper office space with multiple employees.

real_qa.q: What was Michael Dell's original business model when he started in his dorm room at UT Austin?
real_qa.r: Dell began by buying new computers and upgrading them with more memory and hard drives. The main business became putting hard drives into IBM computers that originally had no hard disk drives, upgrading them from two 160K or 320K floppy disk drives to a 10 megabyte hard drive. He advertised in local newspapers, bid on state contracts, and sold to universities, doctors, lawyers, and architects.
real_qa.requete: Dell Computer dorm room hard drive upgrades business model

real_qa.q: How much money was Michael Dell making per month while operating from his dorm room?
real_qa.r: Michael Dell was doing between $50,000 to $80,000 a month in business when he was in his dorm room at UT Austin. This prompted his parents in late 1983 to become upset and demand he stop the business to focus on his studies, though after 10 days he realized this was more than a hobby and negotiated with them to continue.
real_qa.requete: Michael Dell dorm room $50000 $80000 monthly revenue

guest.bio_context: Michael Dell grew up in Houston in the 1970s, where his father was a doctor and his mother was a financial consultant. As a high school student, he made over $18,000 selling newspaper subscriptions by using public marriage registry data. He attended the University of Texas at Austin as a pre-med major but began building computers in his dorm room in 1983, eventually launching Dell Computer Corporation.
